title: Ethiopian Zigni (Eritrean Beef Wat)
community: Northern Ethiopia and Eritrea — the Tigrinya spiced beef stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Tigrinya Zigni — the Northern Ethiopian and Eritrean version of beef wat. Made with a slightly different spice balance (more cardamom and cloves than southern versions), served with injera and tigrinya accompaniments. The beloved beef stew of the Tigrinya-speaking north.
longDesc: Zigni is the Tigrinya-speaking community's Key Wat — similar in technique but distinguished by a different spice balance that reflects the northern highland tradition. The cardamom and cloves are more prominent; the berbere slightly different in composition from southern blends.
steps: Add kibbeh. Add berbere, cardamom, and cloves. Toast 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
chefTips: The cardamom and cloves distinguish zigni from other Key Wats.
Same dry-caramelise technique — this never changes.
commonMistakes: Omitting the cardamom — the northern spice balance is the point.
cookingScience: See ETH021 for Key Wat cooking science. The addition of cardamom (1,8-cineole) and cloves (eugenol) adds two distinctive aromatic compounds to the berbere base — producing a more complex, more fragrant result than southern Key Wat alone.
culturalNote: Zigni is the taste of Tigray and Eritrea — the beef wat that defines the northern highland table. The cardamom note is immediately recognisable to those who know it.
